# Sirach Chapter 21 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 21 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**21:1** My child, have you sinned? Do not do so again, and pray concerning your former sins that they may be forgiven.

**21:2** Flee from sin as from a serpent, for if you draw near it will bite you; its teeth are like the teeth of a lion, destroying the souls of men.

**21:3** All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword; its wound cannot be healed.

**21:4** Terror and violence lay waste to wealth; thus the house of the proud will be devastated.

**21:5** The prayer of the poor man reaches to the ears of God, and his judgment comes quickly.

**21:6** The one who hates rebuke walks in the path of a sinner, but the one who fears the LORD turns back in his heart.

**21:7** A person mighty in tongue is known from afar, but the sensible man knows when he has stumbled.

**21:8** Whoever builds his house with the money of others is like one who gathers stones for his burial mound in winter.

**21:9** The assembly of the lawless is like gathered tow, and their end is a flame of fire.

**21:10** The way of sinners is leveled with smooth stones, but at its end is the pit of Hades.

**21:11** Whoever keeps the law masters his own thoughts, and the completion of the fear of the LORD is wisdom.

**21:12** One who lacks cleverness cannot be educated; but there is a cleverness that multiplies bitterness.

**21:13** The knowledge of a wise man will increase like a flood, and his counsel is like a living spring.

**21:14** The inner part of a fool is like a broken vessel; he is unable to retain any wisdom.

**21:15** When a man of understanding hears a wise word, he praises it and adds to it; the self-indulgent man hears it and it displeases him, so he throws it behind his back.

**21:16** The discourse of a fool is like a burden on a journey, but grace is found upon the lips of a prudent man.

**21:17** The utterance of a sensible man is sought out in the assembly, and his words are pondered in the heart.

**21:18** Wisdom is like a ruined house to a fool, and the knowledge of the senseless is talk unexamined.

**21:19** Instruction is like fetters on the feet of the foolish, and like manacles on the right hand.

**21:20** A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a clever man smiles only quietly.

**21:21** Instruction is like an ornament of gold to a sensible man, and like a bracelet on his right arm.

**21:22** The foot of a fool rushes into a house, but a man of experience holds back respectfully from entering.

**21:23** A foolish person peers into a house through the door, but a well-disciplined man remains outside.

**21:24** It is ill-bred to eavesdrop at the door, but the discreet person is grieved by such dishonor.

**21:25** The lips of arrogant people speak of others' affairs, but the words of the prudent are weighed in the balance.

**21:26** The heart of fools is in their mouth, but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.

**21:27** When an ungodly man curses his adversary, he curses his own soul.

**21:28** A whisperer defiles his own soul and is hated wherever he dwells as a stranger.
